component.name: SnapShotKit
component.summary: Capture a region of the screen and annotate it

description.p: SnapShotKit captures the whole screen the moment you press the key, then lets you choose a region from the frozen image. Nothing moves under the cursor while you aim, because what you are aiming at is already a photograph.
The result opens in an editor with arrows, boxes, blur, text and numbered markers, and is filed in a library grouped by day.

Annotations are kept as objects alongside the untouched capture, so anything drawn can be moved, restyled or removed next week, and the picture underneath is never modified. Exporting to PNG, JPEG or WebP renders the document rather than being the document, and asks first what the file should be and where it goes.

ul.li: Region selection on a frozen screen, with a magnifier for pixel-accurate edges
Arrows, boxes, blur, text and numbered markers, all editable after the fact
Blur that obscures the picture without ever covering the annotations over it
A library of past captures, grouped by day
Any image opened from the file manager, wrapped in a snapshot and annotated the same way
Export to PNG, JPEG or WebP, with transparency, compression and quality settings
Copy the annotated capture straight to the clipboard

description.p: SnapShotKit is free to use while it is pre-1.0. From version 1.0.0 it will cost 15 euro, paid once, with updates included and no subscription. The source stays published either way.

description.p: Capture a window by clicking it, or follow a region while it scrolls. More to draw with, pictures that can be pasted, cropped and printed, and packages for Debian, Ubuntu and any other GNOME desktop.

ul.li: Pick a window to capture by clicking it, or follow a region while it is scrolled and join it into one picture
Lines, ellipses, highlights, a pen, a spotlight, a magnifying lens, callouts, and stronger ways of hiding
Take a colour from the picture, and nudge the selection with the arrow keys
Paste pictures onto the canvas, flip them, and crop or cut any one of them
Open any image, and export as WebP
Print from a dialog that shows the page, through CUPS or to a PDF
Styles and settings in a sidebar, and a recent strip that slides up and can copy, pin and delete captures
Packages for Debian 13 and Ubuntu 25.04 onwards, an AppImage, and arm64 builds
From this version SnapShotKit is source-available rather than GPL, and free to use until 1.0.0
